 Taylor Ardrey USA TODAY Updated Nov. 10, 2026, 10:04 a.m. ET Hear this story Honda is recalling over 635,000 vehicles due to a defect that could cause a loss of power steering assist.
 A  recall notice  posted by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration explained that the issue in certain vehicles could cause motorists to lose control of the vehicle, raising the risk of injury or a crash.
 "The software for the electric power steering (EPS) assist may cause the EPS system to enter a failsafe mode, resulting in a loss of power steering assist," the agency stated.
 Here's what we know about the models included in the recall and what car owners should do next.
 Ford recalls over 36K vehicles. See the affected model 
 Which models are included in the Honda recall?
 According to the NHTSA, 635,808 vehicles are potentially affected. The models included are:
 2021-2025 Acura TLX
 2022-2024 Acura MDX
 2023-2025 Honda Pilot
 The recall numbers are KQB and TQA. Per the safety recall report , Honda has received one report of an injury and no reports of deaths connected to this recall between May 2022 and October 22, 2026.

See the affected models What should car owners do if they have a recalled Honda vehicle?
 Car owners are advised to take their car to the dealership, where the electric power steering assist will be updated. The service is free of charge.
 Notification letters will be sent to owners on Dec. 14.
 Honda can be reached at 866-784-1870.
